review_notes: I read the whole target file, the generic transport API in GradedProjIso.lean (its simp lemmas `projectiveSpectrumEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom_apply` and `projClosedPointsEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom_apply_coe`), and the downstream uses in SymmetricAlgebraClosedPoint.lean. The existing `_apply` simp lemmas for the linear-equivalence transports are rfl specializations. They do not compete with the generic lemmas, because the target defs are distinct heads, and I found no loop. The one concrete gap is that the polynomial-presentation closed-point equivalence has no simp lemma, although its siblings do. A scheme-level `.hom` lemma for the two `Proj` isomorphisms is also missing. I could not run Lean, so the finding is about missing coverage, not an observed simp failure.

findings.problem: This def is the only transport equivalence in the file with no simp or apply lemma. `symmetricAlgebraProjectiveSpectrumEquivOfLinearEquiv` and `symmetricAlgebraProjClosedPointsEquivOfLinearEquiv` both get a `@[simp] ..._apply` lemma, and the generic `projClosedPointsEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom` has `_apply_coe`. Because the target def is a new head symbol, the generic simp lemma cannot fire on `(mvPolynomialProjClosedPointsEquivSymmetricAlgebra b p).1`. Such a term has no simp normal form and can only be reduced by unfolding. Downstream, `projectivizationEquivSymmetricAlgebraClosedPointsOfBasis_mk` in SymmetricAlgebraClosedPoint.lean (about line 249) is closed with a bare `rfl` through this def, so it relies on defeq unfolding of the whole chain instead of a rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: Add, next to the def, `@[simp] theorem mvPolynomialProjClosedPointsEquivSymmetricAlgebra_apply_coe (b : Module.Basis I R M) (p : closedPoints (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule I R))) : (mvPolynomialProjClosedPointsEquivSymmetricAlgebra b p).1 = ProjectiveSpectrum.comapFun (SymmetricAlgebra.equivMvPolynomialGradedHom b).toGradedRingHom (irrelevant_le_map_of_comp_eq_id ... (symmetricAlgebraGradedHom_comp_mvPolynomialGradedHom b)) p.1 := rfl`. This mirrors the existing `symmetricAlgebraProjClosedPointsEquivOfLinearEquiv_apply_coe` at line 120.
findings.benefit: Users and downstream proofs get the same rewriting interface for the polynomial-presentation transport as for the linear-equivalence transport. They can then use `simp` or `rw` on closed-point images instead of unfolding the def or relying on `rfl`.
